title: Compass of customer contrails and feature docket
body:
Purpose: quick, synthesis-first read for product + eng about recent customer threads (Nov 2026 - Jan 2027). This is intentionally messy — meant for fast triage, not an exec brief.

Topline takeaway (one line): customers are asking for two cheap operational controls (per-route cost attribution + predictable cold-start routing) and one medium-effort UX improvement (streamlined model-fallback visibility) that together would materially reduce panic pages and demo friction.

Signal provenance (samples):
- Enterprise retail customer A: reported repeated surprise billing spikes tied to background embedding refresh jobs (support tickets 9432, 9491). Quote: "We didn’t realize the embed-refreshs were counted as production tokens — blew our monthly forecast."
- Mid-market analytics startup B: observed 600ms tail latency increase when low-QPS routes hit autoscale cold pool in EU region (perf thread in Slack #sre-prod, ticket 9578).
- Platform team customer C (private deployment): wants a health endpoint that returns model variant + quantization profile; currently need to SSH to infra node.
- Several smaller customers requested the Console show the last-successful-model-reload timestamp and the active fallback chain per route (feature requests filed in Linear: CS-2183, CS-2201).

Compact themes (clustered):
1) Billing visibility & attribution (high frequency, medium pain)
   - Problem: hidden background / batch operations showing up under same usage bucket as interactive requests; customers unclear which routes produced cost.
   - Representative asks: per-route token breakdown, ability to tag requests for internal cost centers, and a non-technical CSV export of route-level monthly cost.
   - Quick win suggestion: add a per-route tag header (x-rw-cost-tag) that appears in billing UI and a CSV that maps tags -> monthly spend. Low infra change, mostly UI and billing export.

2) Predictable cold-starts & routing (medium frequency, high pain for latency-sensitive apps)
   - Problem: unpredictable tail latency when traffic moves between routing tiers or when autoscale spins new workers; customers want SLO promises or clearer routing policies.
   - Representative asks: explicit route config to prefer warm pool (dedicated) until X QPS, and graceful fallback that serves a lower-capacity variant instead of waiting for new GPUs.
   - Quick win suggestion: expose a per-route "preferred pool" toggle (hosted vs dedicated), and a 2-stage fallback UI where product recommends a compatible lower-cost model variant to return immediately while the main variant warms up.

3) Model-fallback visibility & audit (lower frequency, high severity when it happens)
   - Problem: teams saw wrong-quality outputs after automatic fallback and had no way to correlate the degraded responses to the fallback event.
   - Representative asks: signal in API response that a fallback was used, retention of fallback events in Console trace, alerting when fallback-to-variant X increases > threshold.
   - Quick win suggestion: add a response header (x-rw-fallback: variant-id) and a Console timeline widget that flags fallback intervals.

Micro-feature docket (actionable items, rough cost/impact):
- Add x-rw-cost-tag request header + billing CSV export (effort: 2 sprint dev + 1 sprint billing join; impact: high for chargeback usecases). Owner: CS + Billing + API product.
- Per-route preferred pool toggle & optional warm-reserve flag (effort: 3 sprints infra + 2 sprints console; impact: medium-high). Owner: infra-routing + product-dedicated.
- Response fallback header + Console fallback timeline (effort: 1 sprint API + 1 sprint UI; impact: high for diagnosis). Owner: product-hosted-api + observability.
- Non-technical monthly route-cost CSV (effort: 1 sprint UI + small billing export; impact: medium). Owner: billing + console-ux.
- Health endpoint enhancement for private deployments returning model variant and quantization metadata (effort: small for private package, 1 sprint; impact: medium). Owner: private-deployments + solutions-eng.

Risk/unknowns to validate quickly:
- Does the billing stack currently support tagging at the request level without expensive rework? (ask billing infra: Diego).
- Will exposing quantization/profile data in health endpoints leak sensitive internal model telemetry? (security review needed).
- Are there hard compatibility constraints that prevent offering immediate lower-quality fallbacks for some model architectures (ask applied-ml).

Customer quotes and quick snacks to keep product meetings grounded:
- "If we could just download a CSV and show it to our finance team they'd stop escalating tickets every month." — finance lead, Retail A.
- "We need to know when a response is from a fallback. We spent an afternoon chasing a hallucination that was actually a fallback to an older model." — ML Platform Engineer, Startup B.
- "Private deployment: exposing the model id in health checks would save my team hours of debugging. We run this on-airgap and can't use the control plane for simple checks." — Solutions architect, Customer C.

Immediate next steps (week 1):
- Triage call with Billing, Infra-routing, and Product-hosted-api (owner: Aisha) — propose Wed 2027-02-03. Agenda: feasibility of request-level tags, rough infra cost, and priority for CSV export.
- Quick design spike (2 days) for fallback header + Console timeline prototype (owner: Samira).
- Security assessment kickoff for private health endpoint change (owner: Lena).

Open questions / To discuss in triage:
- Should cost tags be free-form strings or from a managed taxonomy? Tradeoffs: flexibility vs consistent chargeback.
- Do we surface fallback events by default in hosted or make it opt-in for privacy/compliance?
- Can we bundle per-route cost CSV into the existing billing export flow or does it need a new pipeline?

Notes to self (scratchpad):
- Cross-ref: look at tickets 9432, 9491, 9578 before triage call.
- Prep two quick mockups: 1) Console cost-table with tag filter; 2) Console timeline with fallback badges.
- Slack thread to start: #cs-billing-asks and ping Diego, Priya from Billing.

Appendix (raw snippets from threads):
- Support 9491: "token usage spike on 2026-12-05 15:22 — traced to nightly refresh job that ran without cost tag."
- Slack SRE: "cold starts happen mostly when traffic moves across AZs — can we bias routing to preserve warm instances?"

Estimated first-release scope (MVP): fallback header + Console timeline + per-route cost header + CSV export. Target: ship in next quarter if we greenlight infra spike now.

If you want a pared-down slide version for product review, tell me which owners to call out and I’ll sketch 3 slides: problem, MVP plan, and ROI estimate.

-- Aisha
